A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMAD research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original nuScenes results for DMAD and SparseDMAD, including perception, prediction, planning, occupancy prediction, and ablation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds closed-loop NeuroNCAP evaluation, further ablations, attention visualizations, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The two decoders, separate motion and semantic queries, gradient-free reference updates, trajectory-derived velocity, and query propagation are retained. The additional equations and baseline-specific implementation descriptions document the existing approach rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 extends open-loop nuScenes evaluation to closed-loop NeuroNCAP scenes with inserted stationary, frontal, and side safety-critical objects. This adds materially different environmental conditions and planning requirements while retaining the original task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 10–11 add evaluated comparison variants involving object-motion and motion-map interactions and alternative velocity estimators. The named benchmark baselines remain unchanged, and the new NeuroNCAP comparison reuses UniAD and SparseDrive.

E3.justification: v3 introduces closed-loop testing with NeuroNCAP scores based on collisions and impact speeds, alongside controlled interaction and velocity-estimation experiments. Existing training stages and queue lengths are retained. Reported parameter totals are revised without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices H–J add tests of alternative query interactions and four velocity-estimation designs, layer-wise attention heatmaps, and DMAD failure cases. These investigate the separation mechanism, velocity design, and failure behavior; the earlier decoder, queue-length, and prediction-horizon ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting and introduce no statistical uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports closed-loop results, including average collision rates of 60.4% for UniAD versus 50.1% for DMAD. Tables 10–11 and the new visualizations add diagnostic findings. Original nuScenes task scores remain unchanged, but UniAD's reported size changes from 135.0M to 127.3M, raising the stated DMAD parameter overhead from 5.4M to 13.1M.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix C corrects the Bayes-filter posterior equation from equality to proportionality and changes the latest measurement from z_(t-1) to z_t. The additional prediction and tracking equations largely formalize procedures already described in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal divide-and-merge contributions are retained. The conclusion now explicitly qualifies applicability: architectures without query propagation, such as VAD, cannot use the approach without major redesign.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability and failure limitations, including dependence on query propagation and failures involving lane placement, drivable areas, overtaking, and reversing. It also explains the new interaction and velocity ablations, interprets attention patterns, and expands the rationale connecting intermediate-task learning to planning.

D1.justification: New Appendix E specifies separate DMAD and SparseDMAD implementations, including layer sequences, attention heads, embedding and FFN dimensions, dropout, sampling points, and trajectory MLPs. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures. New captions also explain code-version differences behind reported comparisons; the method's code link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds NeuroNCAP and ALVINN citations and an Appendix A discussion positioning the contribution as improving the use of existing intermediate tasks. The earlier related-work survey and principal novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main Sections 1–5 structure are preserved. Changes include localized language edits, expanded prediction and tracking explanations, a revised visualization narrative, and expanded, lettered appendices.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column TMLR layout, adds three tables and Figures 7–19, and moves the earlier appendix collision comparison into the main text as Figure 5. Existing SHAP plots and appendix ablation tables are retained under new numbering; prediction and planning tables also revise highlighting and remove percentage annotations.

improvement.justification: v2 supported planning benefits through open-loop scores and selected collision examples. v3 adds closed-loop safety testing, targeted mechanism ablations, detailed implementation guidance, and explicit failure and applicability limits. Together these substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility. The Bayes-filter and parameter-count corrections also improve reporting accuracy.
